- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The trap-jaw ant (Odontomachus bauri) can close its mandibles at speeds of up to 145 meters per second (328 miles per hour) and generate forces of up to 300 times its body weight.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The mantis shrimp (Stomatopoda) can generate forces of up to 1,500 newtons, or about 335 times its body weight.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other examples of animals that generate impressive amounts of force or power relative to their size include the pistol shrimp, the chameleon, and the hummingbird.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The amount of force or power an animal can generate is dependent on its specific adaptations and the context in which it is applied.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cutting through stone would likely require a sustained effort over a relatively long period of time, which would be challenging for an animal to maintain.
- [USER] Asked if there are any animals that are statistical outliers compared to other creatures in any field.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus) is the fastest animal on the planet, capable of diving at speeds of up to 389 km/h (242 mph).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The tardigrade (water bear) can survive extreme conditions, including extreme temperatures, pressures, radiation levels, and the vacuum of space.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The electric eel (Electrophorus electricus) can generate electric shocks of up to 600 volts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The axolotl (Ambystoma mexicanum) is capable of regenerating lost limbs, spinal cord, heart tissue, and parts of its brain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These animals demonstrate the incredible diversity and adaptability of life on Earth and provide inspiration for scientists and researchers.
